nodes.label: AgenticWorkspace
nodes.description:
A workspace in which an AI agent can re-run an Activity, plus the prompt that asks it to. This is the agentic counterpart of the executable provenance an Activity already carries: `command` and `container_image` tell a machine how to replay a step, while `regeneration_prompt` and `workspace_url` tell an agent how to.
It is typed `prov:Plan` because that is what it is in PROV terms — a description of intended execution, not the execution itself. The run remains the Activity; this is the recipe the agent follows. Keeping them separate matters: re-running a plan produces a NEW Activity, and conflating the two would make a regenerated result indistinguishable from the original.
WARNING ON REPRODUCIBILITY. A prompt is not a deterministic replay mechanism. The same prompt, workspace, and model can yield a different result run to run. Treat `regeneration_prompt` as documentation of intent that a human or agent can act on, NOT as a guarantee of bit-identical output — that is what `command` plus `container_image` plus `code_version` are for. Record the model and version actually used so a divergent re-run can at least be explained.

nodes.label: GeneProgram
nodes.description: A Set whose members are genes that co-vary as a coordinated unit and together carry out a biological process — a factor from matrix factorization (cNMF, NMF, Spectra, WGCNA) or a curated gene module. nodes.label: DAPPER - NIH Dataset Attribution and Provenance Profile
nodes.description:
A LinkML data model for DAPPER, the NIH Dataset Attribution and Provenance Profile. Every dataset returned through an NIH MCP server should carry enough structured metadata for an AI system to cite the dataset, identify its creators, link to the primary publication, report the NIH grant/award that supported it, and describe the provenance of the returned result. The profile's core covers citation/funding/provenance (JSON-LD + DataCite + PROV-O + schema.org) plus GA4GH DRS object identity, DUO data-use terms, RO-Crate packaging, and BioCompute/IEEE-2791 executable workflow provenance.
On top of that core, the profile adds six further blocks:

  DISMECH HARMONIZATION. Cross-walk mappings onto the Monarch Initiative
    DISMECH disease-pathophysiology schema
    (https://w3id.org/monarch-initiative/dismech), so the two models stay
    harmonized without either one forking the other. DISMECH is mirrored
    verbatim from upstream and is NOT edited; all harmonization lives here
    as `exact_mappings` / `close_mappings` plus a `DismechLinked` mixin
    carrying pointers. Reuse, don't reinvent.

  NANOPUBLICATION. The nanopublication model as used by the Nanodash /
    Knowledge Pixels stack: the Head/assertion/provenance/pubinfo quad and
    the npx signature + lifecycle (supersedes / retracts / introduces)
    terms. Lets a DAPPER object be emitted as, or minted from, a signed
    nanopublication.

  AGENTIC REPLAY. `AgenticWorkspace` — the workspace and prompt an
    AI agent can use to re-run an `Activity`. The executable provenance an
    Activity carries (`command`, `container_image`, `code_version`) is
    the machine replay path; this is the agentic one, alongside it rather
    than instead of it. A prompt is NOT a deterministic replay mechanism,
    so the two are deliberately not interchangeable.

  HYPOTHESIS. A FAIR-digital-object hypothesis — the REVEAL output — as
    a gene -> mechanism -> disease causal chain. Structurally compatible
    with dismech.monarchinitiative.org (it reuses DISMECH's hypothesis
    grouping, causal-edge, and evidence shapes and its CausalLinkTypeEnum
    values verbatim) and carries full attribution/provenance by mixing in
    `ProvenancedResource`, so a hypothesis is citable exactly like a
    dataset.

  SINGLE-CELL. `GeneProgram` — a coordinated pattern of gene activity
    representing a biological process, e.g. a factor from cNMF/NMF/
    Spectra/WGCNA or a curated gene module — extends `Set` the same way
    `GeneSet` does, with genes as members. `CellState` is the cellular
    phenotype defined by the combination of `GeneProgram`s active in a
    cell (or cell population) at once, as distinct from a cell TYPE (a
    Cell Ontology class), which is what lineage a cell belongs to rather
    than what functional state it is in.

The schema is shaped as a Dock knowledge graph: NIH resources, agents, awards, publications, hypotheses, and nanopublications are Node entities; attribution, provenance, and causal assertions are Edge relationships.

nodes.label: Schema model boundary
nodes.rationale: Keep schema modules, model examples, converters, and model documentation under schema/; factor common vocabulary only when a second consumer exists.

nodes.label: DAPPER-ID-1
nodes.rationale: Compute class-qualified sha512t24u addresses from identity fields; exclude timestamps, signatures, and mirror observations so incidental processing does not change identity. IDs must be minted rather than written by hand.

nodes.label: Portal freshness invariant
nodes.rationale: Regenerate the committed portal from schema/dapper.yaml and examples during CI; fail deployment if it differs so rendered identifiers cannot silently drift from the schema.

nodes.label: Provenance source of truth
nodes.rationale: The standalone geneset.provenance.json contains both HZ2 analysis steps; metadata-sidecar lineage collapses these and should not be migrated as a duplicate lossy graph.

nodes.label: Rebasing
nodes.rationale: Rewrite local storage prefixes into public or remote URI prefixes and recompute source content IDs before conversion; this is distinct from DAPPER mirror governance and requires no new schema structure.

nodes.label: Mirror attribution invariant
nodes.rationale: Downstream caches may append provenance but cannot rewrite authoritative NIH attribution.

nodes.label: NIH attribution overlay
nodes.rationale: dig.geneset does not carry authoritative NIH creators, awards, publications, or citation; supply these through --overlay rather than inventing them during conversion.

nodes.label: Manifest-backed distribution
nodes.rationale: A multi-file Spark output is a dataset with manifest-based versioning represented by a single DrsObject; reuse Dataset, Activity, and DrsObject rather than adding a bottom-line class or per-variant nodes.

nodes.label: Human-curated provenance
nodes.rationale: A curated record can identify a curator using was_attributed_to without inventing a generating Activity. Machine-derived GenePrograms use the same Used and WasGeneratedBy edges as GeneSet.

nodes.label: Cell type versus cell state
nodes.rationale: CellState represents functional phenotype determined by active GenePrograms; a Cell Ontology cell type names lineage. Example program associations are illustrative, not a biological assertion about ductal identity.

nodes.label: Continuous cell-state activity
nodes.rationale: Interpret marker programs as within-cell-type gradients rather than mutually exclusive state probabilities; hard calls require separate score-distribution validation.

nodes.label: Unified claim provenance graph
nodes.rationale: NanopubProvenance.generated_by_activity targets an Activity already connected to source files by Used and WasGeneratedBy; evidence retrieval traverses one graph without a separate bridge model.

nodes.label: Machine replay
nodes.rationale: Use Activity command, code_version, and container_image for exact reproducibility; an agentic rerun is a separate recorded analysis rather than a determinism guarantee.

nodes.label: File converter classification
nodes.rationale: Nonempty c2m2_properties select C2M2File; source File nodes without them become generic File records. Generic fields are read directly, and location joins the metadata-sidecar path or local_path for SHA-256.

nodes.label: Trusty URI RA
nodes.rationale: A versioned content address covers a canonical RDF dataset and identifies the full immutable publication package, not serialization bytes or only its assertion.

nodes.label: Content integrity verification
nodes.rationale: A hash verifies immutable content independently of the mirror serving it; signatures separately prove control of a key.

nodes.label: Nanopublication publication transformation
nodes.rationale: Validate, serialize four RDF graphs, sign and mint with maintained tooling, independently verify, and store transformation provenance; publication is separate from schema validation.

nodes.label: Immutable publication evolution
nodes.rationale: Corrections receive new identifiers and link to previous nanopublications with supersession or retraction statements.

nodes.label: Mirror provenance invariant
nodes.rationale: Mirrors cannot modify authoritative provenance under an existing verified identity; append information using a separate object related to the original.

nodes.norm_label: dataset provenance and mirroring graph example

nodes.label: Positionally paired members and weights
nodes.rationale: members[i] and member_weights[i] describe the same gene from an NMF loading matrix.

nodes.label: Shared agentic replay workspace
nodes.rationale: One illustrative workspace can rerun both pipeline steps while each Activity retains command and code version for exact replay; regenerated outputs create new provenance.

nodes.label: Standalone PEP-723 script environment
nodes.rationale: Tests assemble pytest with the standalone scripts dependencies in one uv environment; normal script use requires no package installation.

nodes.label: DAPPER-ID-1
nodes.rationale: An identifier names one metadata record, not its underlying file bytes; class and hashable content determine the digest while volatile context is excluded.

nodes.label: Metadata record identity
nodes.rationale: Different descriptions of the same biological resource receive different IDs; file checksums determine byte equality separately.

nodes.label: Canonical RDF digest input
nodes.rationale: Canonicalized RDF is serialized to N-Triples, sorted, newline-joined, and UTF-8 encoded to ensure insertion-order independence.

nodes.label: Slot-name identity predicates
nodes.rationale: Slot names distinguish fields sharing an ontology URI and prevent ontology remapping from changing identifiers.

nodes.label: Ordered list identity
nodes.rationale: An element index is part of each digest predicate, preserving citation-bearing author order.

nodes.label: Volatile reference exclusion
nodes.rationale: Mark references to volatile objects unhashable, not the volatile objects own content; otherwise all instances of the latter collapse to one digest.

nodes.label: Acyclic hash dependency graph
nodes.rationale: Unhashable back-references break nanopublication reference cycles so identifiers can be assigned bottom up.

nodes.label: Permanent identity test vectors
nodes.rationale: Published identifiers depend on permanent vectors; algorithm changes require a new DAPPER-ID profile and prefix rather than modified vectors.

nodes.label: Out-of-band profile version
nodes.rationale: Current IDs encode class and digest but no in-band algorithm version; HashableNode records the profile and future algorithms must use a new prefix.

nodes.label: Automatically discovered example coverage
nodes.rationale: Glob every examples YAML file so new or previously omitted examples receive identifier and reference checks.

nodes.label: Identity behavior regression tests
nodes.rationale: Pin individual identity properties as well as frozen-vector outcomes so regressions explain why an identifier moved.

nodes.label: DOC_GROUPS coverage
nodes.rationale: Every Node class needs a grouped-document key shared by the portal and identifier minter.

nodes.label: File and DRS composition
nodes.rationale: A File describes a single artifact in provenance and may reference one or more DRS blob representations. DrsObject remains separate because DRS can also represent bundles; a containing bundle is not a representation of one file. Dataset distributions retain their separate has_drs_object semantics.

nodes.label: Access-independent file identity
nodes.rationale: File.location and File.drs_representation are unhashable access metadata; relocating or registering a file leaves its metadata-record ID unchanged. Checksums and other file metadata remain hashable; C2M2File.local_id retains its existing hashable source-identifier semantics.

nodes.label: Cross-record checksum agreement
nodes.rationale: Linked File and DRS records should agree on bytes through size and checksums, but LinkML only validates individual record shapes. Compare matching algorithms after normalizing encodings: File MD5 is base64, DRS MD5 is hex, and both SHA-256 fields are hex.

nodes.label: Generic file conversion
nodes.rationale: Select C2M2File for nonempty source c2m2_properties and File otherwise; read generic fields directly and use location to join sidecar paths for SHA-256.

nodes.label: Intermediate file
nodes.rationale: One activity produces the normalized matrix and another consumes that same File via ordinary PROV edges. Intermediate is its position in the graph; an optional DRS node exposes the same bytes. All example nodes are synthetic.

nodes.label: Class-qualified file identity
nodes.rationale: DAPPER IDs identify metadata records and include the full class name. Changing File to C2M2File changes the ID even for identical bytes.

nodes.label: File regression coverage
nodes.rationale: test_files.py covers generic intermediates, ID stability across relocation and DRS registration, converter provenance, and portal inheritance.
